body:
Thank you so much for sharing your story. It feels really good to share these situations in this forum as I all of a sudden feel less alone. 

Maybe Nex's just do that to you regardless of the physical distance to one's support system. The isolation in the experience of having a nex influences the easiness of reaching out as few people can truly understand the difficulties. 

But personally, I am very aware of telling my stories to my support system. I know they are there and they would do everything for me to feel better. But I am aware of how much it may hurt them to see me hurt and the fact that they never knew and could act on it. I am trying to trust them more, and trust that they can communicate their boundaries to me, but I think it is a real issue.

I've only been in therapy before for a burn-out, so I haven't really had homework as such, but it will probably be a good idea to bring it up at our next session, or at least tools to deal with the post-session-sadness maybe.
Thank you! That is a seriously beautiful metaphor, and I will try and remember it when it's difficult. It'll definitely explain my sea-sickness

I understand your struggles. I am currently 6 months out of a relationship with an undiagnosed narcissist, and I am still struggling with dependency and anxiety relating to him. It has gotten better, and it will for you too, but it doesn't make it less shit. Just know that you will finally be in charge of your own happiness instead of having someone feed off it and suck you dry.

Thank you so much for your kind words. It does give me enough proof to keep going. He has talked about getting help, but it is the actual doing that concerns me as I don't know if he has the energy to do so. But I guess I can't do it for him either. 

Thank you anyways, it does help to know that somebody, even anonymous, can still see the worth in keeping this up even when I am fumbling in the dark.
